newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian defence ministers visit Khmer Rouge base.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian defence ministers visit Khmer Rouge base.

text.p: Cambodia's two defence ministers on Thursday visited the Pailin base of dissident Khmer Rouge guerrillas to discuss their terms for a speedy merger of government and rebel forces, military officials said.

A defence ministry spokesman said Tea Banh and Tea Chamrath flew by helicopter to the northwest border town, whose guerrilla garrison broke with hardline Khmer Rouge supporters of Pol Pot in August and pledged alliance to Ieng Sary.

The co-ministers, accompanied by armed forces Chief of Staff General Ke Kim Yan and other senior officers, left from the city of Battambang "to visit our brothers and sisters, the Khmer Rouge separatists", said Chum Sambath, who gave no further details.

Reached after the meeting, Tea Banh told Reuters: "I met Ieng Sary this morning to push forward some tasks, such as merging the forces and to discuss technical issues -- how to link up. The meeting went well. Everything was agreed."

It was the ministers first visit to territory commanded by the Ieng Sary loyalists. They had forged a ceasefire and agreed to set up a military working group to pursue full reconciliation during a September 5 meeting in Thailand with Ieng Sary, foreign minster during the brutal 1975-79 Khmer Rouge regime of Pol Pot.

The peace process stalled until King Norodom Sihanouk on September 14 granted Ieng Sary an amnesty from his 1979 death sentence in absentia for his role in the genocide of more than one million people in the late 1970s.

When the military working group met a few days later in Pailin, Ei Chien and other commanders demanded top central command posts in the armed forces and police and said Pailin should become a province under their control.
The government has rejected handing out very top positions but is ready to offer senior regional military commands and to consider creating a new province around Pailin.

Co-Premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen have insisted that all zones controlled by the guerrillas must come under government administration, and they have told the dissidents to stop delaying the merger of their forces with the government.
Pressure on Ieng Sary and his men to complete the process of reconciliation came earlier this month when more than 1,000 hardline guerrillas agreed to defect to the government.
A report in the Cambodia Daily on Thursday said two more divisions had joined the government in the western province of Pursat. This could not be confirmed.
